w10:2: Paper 99:5–6 · Paper 101:1, 8 · Paper 107 · Paper 108:5 · Paper 110:3 · Paper 111:1–3, 5 · Paper 112:5 · Paper 100:2, 4 · Paper 91:8 · Paper 146:2 · Papers 115–117
w10:3: This week's map — from living religion, through the Adjuster and the soul, to prayer and worship and the God of time
w10:6: If the last two weeks told the outer history of our planet, this week turns to the inner history of a human being. The Urantia Book says that true religion is not an institution or a creed but a personal experience of knowing God as Father. That experience is possible because the Universal Father has sent a fragment of Himself, the Thought Adjuster, to live in the human mind. As mind and Adjuster work together, a soul grows that can survive death, and it grows through prayer, worship, and love of our neighbors. All these small growths are added to the God who is Himself growing in time, the Supreme Being.
w10:11: Picture an old radio. The station broadcasts day and night, but if the dial is slightly off, all that comes through is static. Turn the dial slowly with a fingertip, and at the moment the frequency lines up, a song rises clear out of the crackle. The signal had filled the room all along. What changed was the receiver.
w10:13: The inner story told in The Urantia Book is much like this. God is present in each human mind at this very moment, leading without pause, yet most of the time we miss the music.
w10:15: This week looks at that inner station, the Thought Adjuster; at the soul that grows as it receives the signal; and at prayer and worship, the practice of tuning the dial.
w10:21: The word "religion" usually brings to mind buildings, ceremonies, and doctrines. The Urantia Book reverses the order: the root of religion is the living relationship between one person and God. Paper 99 puts it in a single sentence.
w10:25: Where does this experience take place? Paper 101 answers: not in stirred-up emotion, but in the highest kind of thinking.
w10:31: The intensity of a feeling is not the measure of a religious experience. God meets people in the quiet place where they think about what is right and choose it.
w10:35: The book draws a careful line between belief and faith. Accepting a teaching as true is belief; it becomes faith only when it actually changes the direction of a life.
w10:41: Belief and faith (the author's summary, based on 101:8.1–2)
w10:44: That belief governing the way one lives
w10:46: Can be held by a group
Grows only in the individual heart
w10:49: A creed can be recited together, but no one can have faith on someone else's behalf. What, then, unites people of faith?
w10:53: Paper 103 makes the order of theology and religion plain.
w10:59: None of this means the book regards religious groups as useless. People who share a faith naturally gather, and Paper 99 describes warmly what such a gathering is for.
w10:63: The danger comes when the gathering stiffens into an institution. The same section goes on to give a long list of warnings.
w10:67: And it leaves one short, solid sentence.
w10:71: Living religion and a hardened institution (the author's summary, based on 99:5–6)
w10:78: Fruits of the spirit, brotherly love
w10:81: **A common misunderstanding**: The Urantia Book rejects the church and teaches people to believe on their own.
w10:82: **What The Urantia Book says**: Religious groups have real purposes: worship and education, fellowship and service (99:6.2). What the book warns against is creedal pressure and institutional rigidity. Paper 103 says there is great hope for any church that frees its members from the pressure of creeds (103:5.12).
w10:85: 2. The Thought Adjuster, a Fragment of the Father
w10:87: Farthest Away and Nearest of All
w10:89: In Week 1 we briefly met the phrase "a fragment of God." Paper 107 introduces this fragment in full, and it opens with a striking paradox.
w10:93: "Mystery Monitor" is another name for the Thought Adjuster, and to "indwell" is to live within. The Father at the center of all things is at the same time inside each human mind. Why would He do this? Paper 107 links the gift to the command we saw in Paper 1: "Be you perfect."
w10:97: God did not only give the command; He came down Himself to be our partner in keeping it. Is the Adjuster, then, something like an angel that God created? Paper 107 says no.
w10:101: The Adjuster is not a messenger God sends but a piece of God Himself. A cup of seawater is not the whole ocean, yet it is the very same water. Paper 107 compares the Adjuster's work to a compass.
w10:105: To call God our Father is therefore no mere figure of speech. The Father has actually shared His own spirit with His children. And this guide never fails.
w10:111: The Adjuster is not here to make life comfortable. Paper 108 is clear on this point.
w10:115: A good coach does not make an athlete's day easy. The Adjuster also takes pleasure in our health and happiness (110:1.3), but all of that care gathers toward one end: that we survive forever and grow more and more like God.
w10:117: The trouble is that this leading is hard to hear.
w10:121: This is exactly the radio of the opening story. Does that mean someone who hears poorly has failed?
w10:125: Doubting and wandering are quite different from deliberately turning away. Co-operating with the Adjuster is not a matter of special mystical experiences; it happens in everyday motives and decisions (110:3.6). Nor is it a gloomy self-denial.
w10:131: Paper 107 also mentions an intriguing detail: the Adjuster is called by different names as a person grows older.
w10:135: The Adjuster arrives around the time a child makes the first moral decision, on average just before the sixth birthday (108:2.1). The three names can be read not as a change in the Adjuster but as a deepening relationship between the person and the Adjuster.
w10:137: After telling the whole life of Jesus, the very last paper of the book leaves this task to the people of today.
w10:141: Three names across a lifetime — Thought Changer, Thought Adjuster, Thought Controller (the author's summary, based on 107:0.7 and 108:2.1)
w10:144: **Mystery Monitor**: Another name for the Thought Adjuster, so called because its nature is still veiled in mystery.
w10:145: **Indwelling**: Living within. The Adjuster indwells the human mind, not the brain (110:1.1).
w10:146: **Fusion**: The eternal union of a surviving human soul with the Adjuster. Once fused, the two can never again be separated.
w10:150: **A common misunderstanding**: The Thought Adjuster is just another name for conscience, or for the good thoughts in my own mind.
w10:151: **What The Urantia Book says**: The Adjuster is neither a created being nor part of the human mind; it is a fragment of God Himself (107:1.2). It never overrides the human will but always respects a person's choices (111:1.8), and it works in the conflicts between right and wrong even when the person is not aware of it (108:5.9).
w10:158: The Adjuster works in the human mind. Paper 111 traces where each of three things comes from: the body, the Adjuster, and the mind.
w10:162: Evolution gave the body, and the Father gave the Adjuster. Only the mind, standing between them, is placed "into your hands." Paper 111 pictures the three as a single ship.
w10:166: However skilled the pilot, the captain is the one in command. The Adjuster shows the way, but it is the human will that sets the course. Paper 111 stresses the point again.
w10:172: What, then, is the soul? The Urantia Book says the soul is not handed to us at the start; it grows.
w10:176: The soul is born of the relationship between mind and Adjuster. When two people share a long friendship, the friendship becomes a new reality that belongs to neither one alone but lives between them. Paper 112 calls the soul a "child."
w10:180: How the soul is born — the morontia soul growing out of the relationship between mind and Adjuster (the author's summary, based on 111:1.9, 111:2.4–7 and 112:5.12)
w10:184: What makes the soul grow? Paper 111 looks less at how much a mind knows than at which way it faces.
w10:188: Even with much still unknown and much still lacking, the soul grows as long as it keeps choosing the direction of wanting to know God. And what grows in this way is not lost.
w10:192: The Personality That Does Not Change
w10:194: Paper 112 tells us where this journey begins.
w10:198: What stays the same while the soul grows is personality. Personality is the unique selfhood the Universal Father gives each person, and no two are alike (112:0.12). It is this same "I" that awakens on the mansion worlds after death. There the Adjuster returns and links the old life with the new.
w10:202: Many memories are cleared away like scaffolding once the building is finished, but our relationships with the people we loved remain. The journey after death that we followed in Week 6 has its seed growing here and now, on this earth.
w10:205: **Soul**: The morontia reality born and growing out of the relationship between the mind and the indwelling Adjuster. It survives death.
w10:206: **Morontia**: The level of reality between the material and the spiritual. The soul and the bodies of the mansion worlds belong to it.
w10:207: **Personality**: The unique endowment the Universal Father gives each person, the "I" that remains unchanged in the midst of change.
w10:214: Paper 100 sums up the path of spiritual growth in three steps.
w10:218: We realize that something is missing, we begin to see what the events of life mean, and among them we discover what is truly precious. This growth is not always smooth.
w10:222: A season when faith is shaken need not be seen as failure. Paper 100 says there is a place that does not fall even in such times.
w10:226: The stairway of spiritual growth — from an awakening to needs to a discovery of values (the author's summary, based on 100:2.2 and 100:4.2)
w10:230: The evidence of growth is love. Yet love does not come from resolve alone. Paper 100 offers a very practical path.
w10:234: Paper 100 also traces how understanding ripens into love.
w10:238: Trying to understand the one person who weighs on our mind today is a bigger step than vowing to love all of humanity.
w10:240: Prayer Changes the One Who Prays
w10:242: What is prayer? Paper 91 sets prayer beside magic to show the difference.
w10:246: Magic tries to bend heaven to our will; prayer tries to bend our will to heaven. Paper 91 compares this to a bird's wings.
w10:254: Jesus, too, taught his disciples at length about prayer at Jotapata, a small town in Galilee. One of his main points was this.
w10:258: He also taught them to be silent for a while after praying.
w10:262: If prayer is the time for speaking, silence is the time for listening, the time for tuning the radio dial. As prayer matures, it becomes worship. Prayer still carries something of our own needs; worship asks for nothing and simply delights in God for being God.
w10:266: All this growth comes down to one choice: the choice to do the Father's will. Paper 111 says this choice does not crush the will but uses it most fully.
w10:271: Paul asked, "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?" (1 Corinthians 3:16). Jesus taught his hearers to enter into the closet and pray to the Father "which is in secret" (Matthew 6:6). The Urantia Book explains this "God within" more fully under the name of the Thought Adjuster.
w10:275: **A common misunderstanding**: Prayer is a way of getting what we want, and if we ask long and hard enough, God will change His mind.
w10:276: **What The Urantia Book says**: Prayer changes not God's attitude but ours (146:2.8). God answers the attitude of the soul, not the words (91:8.12). Jesus warned against the habit of praying only in times of trouble, and taught that the one form of prayer suited to all God's children is "Your will be done" (146:2.12).
w10:279: 5. God in Time, the Supreme Being
w10:283: Last of all we meet the least familiar idea of the week. God the Father is eternal and perfect, and He does not grow. Yet The Urantia Book says there is also a God who grows along with the universes of time and space. He is the Supreme Being.
w10:287: "The Supreme" is the book's shorter name for the Supreme Being. Paper 116 observes that an honest look at confused Urantia makes it reasonable to conclude that this world is governed by Creators who are not yet perfect (116:0.2). The universe is not a finished house but a house still being built.
w10:291: The most remarkable thing about this teaching is that human choices really are added to that growth.
w10:295: Paper 115 briefly shows how our standing differs before the Father and before the Supreme.
w10:299: God the Father and God the Supreme (the author's summary, based on 115:0.1, 117:2.1 and 117:6.21–23)
w10:304: In the hearts of all other people
w10:305: Can be found by one person
w10:309: Where, then, do we meet the Supreme? Paper 117 answers this way.
w10:313: The way to the Father turns inward; the way to the Supreme turns outward, toward our neighbors. The two ways join in one great circle.
w10:317: Paper 117 then shows what travels along that avenue.
w10:321: Love is not a still pond but a flowing river. The love we receive from the Father becomes ours only as we let it flow on to others. And as that flow builds up, the God of time grows.
w10:323: The great circuit of love — love that comes from the Father and passes through our neighbors to the Supreme (the author's summary, based on 117:6.10)
w10:325: This discovery does not come all at once.
w10:329: And those who walk this road are never alone.
w10:333: Within, the Father walks beside us; underfoot, the road itself is the Supreme. Paper 117 reminds us what this whole journey is a search for.
w10:337: This week's study fits into a single sentence: God lives within us, and we meet Him again in our neighbors.
w10:340: **Supreme Being**: The God who grows through experience together with the universes of time and space. Standing alone, He is also called "the Supreme."
w10:341: **God-consciousness**: The experience of becoming aware of the reality of God through the indwelling spirit (103:1.6).
w10:342: **Great circuit of love**: The circle in which the Father's love flows through each person to his or her neighbors and on to the Supreme.
w10:346: True religion is a person's living experience of knowing God as Father and other people as brothers and sisters.
w10:347: Belief accepts a teaching; faith is that belief actually changing a life. When an institution hardens, the power of religion weakens.
w10:348: The Thought Adjuster is not a created being but an actual fragment of the Universal Father, an infallible compass that always points the soul toward God.
w10:349: The soul is not given at the start. It is born as a morontia reality from the relationship between mind and Adjuster, grows, and survives death.
w10:350: Mind is the ship, the Adjuster the pilot, the will the captain. The Adjuster never overrides the human will.
w10:351: Prayer does not change God; it changes us. Worship makes us more and more like the One we worship.
w10:352: The Supreme Being is God growing in time. We meet the Father within ourselves and the Supreme in our neighbors.
w10:356: Of the things you say you "believe," which ones are actually changing the way you live? In light of the distinction in Paper 101, is each of them belief or faith?
w10:357: In the picture of mind as the ship, the Adjuster as the pilot, and the will as the captain (111:1.9), what kind of captain are you right now?
w10:358: If you were to practice "each day you learn to love one more human being" (100:4.6) this week, who would that one person be, and where could you begin?
w10:362: Papers 119–170 — The Creator Becomes a Son of Man: the seven bestowals of Michael and the life of Jesus of Nazareth
w11:1: Part Four The Life and Teachings of Jesus
The Creator Becomes a Son of Man
w11:2: The Creator Becomes a Son of Man
w11:3: Papers 119–120 · Papers 121–127 · Paper 129 · Paper 132 · Paper 134 · Papers 136–137 · Papers 140–142 · Paper 155 · Paper 170
w11:4: This week's map — from the seven bestowals through the Nazareth years, the Mediterranean journey and the baptism in the Jordan, to the gospel of the kingdom of heaven
w11:7: Michael, the Creator Son who made our local universe, becomes its full sovereign only after living seven times in the likeness of the beings he has made. The seventh and last of these bestowals is the life of Jesus of Nazareth. He was born a helpless baby, grew up in an ordinary family, lost his father at fourteen and became the head of the household, and walked the Mediterranean world meeting people one at a time. Beginning his public work with his baptism in the Jordan, he preached a simple gospel: God is the Father of all people, and all people are brothers and sisters. This week follows the main lines of his life and teaching up to the final week.
w11:12: Imagine a doctor who has built a great hospital. No one knows its layout and its medical equipment better than he does. Then one day he puts on a patient's gown and lies down in a bed on the busiest ward. He wants to feel in his own body the groans in the night, the meal gone cold, the long tedium of waiting, and the comfort a single word from the doctor on rounds can bring.
w11:14: The one who knows the hospital and the one who has lain in its beds will run the same hospital differently. The first will be fair. The second will be fair and deeply understanding as well.
w11:16: Part Four of The Urantia Book is the story of the Maker of a universe lying down in that very bed. In Parts One to Three we set out from Paradise and came down through the long history of Nebadon and Urantia. Now all those roads converge on the life of one man.
w11:18: 1. Seven Bestowals — The Seven Steps Michael Took
w11:20: Why a Creator becomes a creature
w11:22: As we saw in Week 5, our local universe of Nebadon was made by the Creator Son Michael. Yet making a universe does not, by itself, give him full sovereignty over it. He must live as one of his own creatures. This act, in which a divine Son humbles himself and enters creature life, is called a **bestowal**. Paper 119 explains its purpose.
w11:26: Even a Son of God learns by experience. Mercy was there from the start, but once it has been lived through, it becomes "understanding mercy."
w11:32: In each bestowal he submitted himself to a different aspect of the will of the Paradise Deities.
w11:36: The stairway runs downward. It begins in the form of a high Son, passes through angel and ascending mortal, and reaches at last mortal flesh, the lowest place among will creatures. And only on that final step does he live the will of the Universal Father directly.
w11:38: Michael's seven bestowals — a stairway descending from the form of a high Son to mortal flesh (arranged by the author from 119:8.4 and 120:0.4)
w11:40: The seven bestowals and the will each followed (119:8.4, 120:0.4)
w11:43: United will of Father, Son, and Spirit
w11:44: Will of the Father and the Son
w11:45: Will of the Father and the Spirit
w11:46: Will of the Son and the Spirit
w11:47: Will of the Infinite Spirit (Conjoint Actor)
w11:49: Jesus, a mortal man on Urantia
w11:53: The celestial beings knew that the seventh bestowal would be made in mortal flesh, but not how. In every earlier bestowal Michael had appeared fully grown.
w11:57: The sovereign of a universe began as a baby who could do nothing for himself. Before he left, his elder brother Immanuel gave him this charge.
w11:61: Here is the key to the whole life of Jesus. His task was to keep his communion with the Father unbroken, and that communion itself became the revelation of the Father. Was Jesus, then, half God and half man? Paper 120 answers plainly.
w11:66: **Bestowal**: a divine Son humbling himself to enter a world and live there in the likeness of its creatures.
w11:67: **Incarnation**: a divine being being born in a human body. How it happens remains an eternal mystery (119:7.5).
w11:68: **Immanuel**: a high being who represents the Paradise Trinity in Nebadon; he looked after the universe while Michael was on his bestowals.
w11:72: Philippians says that Christ "made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men" (Phil. 2:7). Hebrews speaks of a high priest who was "in all points tempted like as we are" and so can be "touched with the feeling of our infirmities" (Heb. 4:15). The Urantia Book's idea of bestowal sets this self-emptying and this sympathy within a cosmic picture of seven steps.
w11:75: 2. The Boy and Carpenter of Nazareth — The Home of Joseph and Mary
w11:79: The age into which Jesus was born was not chosen at random. Rome had bound the Mediterranean into one world, Greek was understood almost everywhere, and good roads and safe seas carried ideas quickly.
w11:83: Yet beneath the outward prosperity, people's souls were hungry. Myths, emperor worship, astrology and the mystery cults pouring in from the East all promised salvation. The book sees even that hunger as part of the preparation for Jesus.
w11:89: A generation worn out by complicated rites was handed the simplest of truths: God is a Father, and we are His children.
w11:93: Jesus was born in Bethlehem on August 21, 7 B.C. The book calls him Joshua ben Joseph, Joshua the son of Joseph. His parents were not remarkable people.
w11:97: Joseph was a quiet, thoughtful carpenter; Mary was cheerful, frank and practical. Their son took different gifts from each.
w11:101: A small episode from about his fifth year foreshadows the faith of his whole life.
w11:107: At thirteen Jesus went up to Jerusalem for his first Passover. Watching the crowds at the temple, his heart filled with compassion, and that night a heavenly messenger came to him for the first time.
w11:113: Right after the call came trial. The book names the hardest time of Jesus' life not as the cross but as his fourteenth and fifteenth years.
w11:117: In September of A.D. 8, Joseph was fatally injured by a falling derrick while working on a building in Sepphoris. Every plan for study in Jerusalem collapsed.
w11:123: From the birth of Ruth, the youngest, until he began his public ministry, he was a father to his brothers and sisters. The first prayer he wrote down for the family later became the Lord's Prayer (126:3.3-4). While working as a carpenter, he weighed every institution in the world by three questions.
w11:127: Readers today can pick up these three questions just as they are. They can be put to the groups we belong to and to the habits and beliefs we hold on to. Paper 127 pictures Jesus at about twenty like this.
w11:131: He skipped no age of life, and every bit of that experience became his own.
w11:135: A timeline of the life of Jesus of Nazareth — from Bethlehem to Bethany (arranged by the author from the dates in Papers 122–168; spacing not to scale)
w11:138: **Joshua ben Joseph**: "Joshua the son of Joseph," the Hebrew name of Jesus.
w11:139: **Son of Man**: the title Jesus chose for himself. At about fifteen he read it in the Book of Enoch and took it to heart (126:3.8).
w11:140: **Thought Adjuster**: the fragment of the Father's spirit we met in Week 10. An Adjuster dwelt in Jesus' human mind too and grew along with him.
w11:143: 3. Walking the Mediterranean World — The Journey to Rome
w11:147: Once his brothers and sisters had found their own way, Jesus left home. From April of A.D. 22 to December of the following year, he served as interpreter and tutor to Gonod, a merchant from India, and his son Ganid, traveling the Mediterranean world by way of Alexandria, Athens and Rome (130:0.1). No one knew who he was. For the celestial watchers, this period was special.
w11:153: In Rome he did not preach. Instead he sat down with people face to face.
w11:157: A single meeting could change a person's life.
w11:161: To a soldier he met by the Tiber he said this.
w11:167: Before the public ministry, there was already a ministry without a name.
w11:169: Not a model but a way
w11:173: That does not mean we are to copy his life detail by detail.
w11:177: We cannot become first-century Galilean carpenters, nor do we need to. But we can live where we are today in the same way he trusted the Father and loved people.
w11:181: In late summer of A.D. 25, Jesus went up Mount Hermon alone and spent six weeks in communion with the Father. In the last week, Satan and Caligastia appeared and offered him compromises.
w11:187: The temptation in the wilderness, which the Gospels place after the baptism, is told in this book as the event on Mount Hermon before the baptism. The Lucifer rebellion we saw in Week 7 was, in effect, settled that day.
w11:190: **A common misunderstanding**: Jesus knew everything from the start, so his human life was only an appearance.
w11:191: **What The Urantia Book says**: Jesus was always both God and man (120:4.3), but he came to realize this gradually in his human mind (120:4.2). During the incarnation he set aside help from beyond the planet of his own choice (120:1.3), and he learned of Gabriel's visit to his mother only on the day of his baptism (126:2.4). He truly learned, struggled and grew.
w11:194: 4. The Baptism in the Jordan and the Public Ministry
w11:198: Even when word came that John was preaching a baptism of repentance in the Jordan, Jesus did not hurry.
w11:202: He did not go to confess his sins.
w11:210: As we saw in Week 10, a mortal who reaches completion fuses with the Thought Adjuster. The celestial onlookers expected exactly that at the Jordan. Something else happened instead.
w11:214: Paper 136 sums up the day briefly.
w11:219: Matthew tells how, as Jesus came up out of the water after his baptism, the heavens opened and a voice said, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Matt. 3:16-17). The Urantia Book explains that the voice was that of the Adjuster who had dwelt in Jesus, now personalized (136:2.5). The temptation in the wilderness (Matt. 4:1-11) is told as the event on Mount Hermon before the baptism (134:8.9).
w11:224: After his baptism Jesus spent forty days alone, thinking over the road ahead. That year he called his first disciples, and on January 12, A.D. 27, he ordained the twelve apostles (140:0.1). Then came the preaching tours of Galilee; the great encampment by the sea at Bethsaida in A.D. 28 (148:0.1); in A.D. 29 the feeding of the five thousand and the crisis at Capernaum, when he refused the crowd that wanted to make him king; the experience on the mount of transfiguration; and in A.D. 30 the Perean mission and the raising of Lazarus at Bethany. Lazarus led the Jerusalem leaders to resolve to put Jesus to death, and the story moves into the final week, which we will see in Week 12.
w11:226: The course of the public ministry — from the baptism to Lazarus (a sketch by the author based on Papers 136–168, not an actual map)
w11:228: Not the same thoughts, but the same spirit
w11:230: The twelve apostles were a mixed band of fishermen, a tax collector and Zealots. One evening at Amathus, when James asked how they could all learn to see alike, Jesus asked him in return when he had ever taught such a thing, and then answered.
w11:234: What he wanted was not uniformity but spiritual unity. People who think differently can still be one if they host the same Father's spirit and seek to do the same will.
w11:236: 5. The Gospel of the Kingdom of Heaven — Fatherhood and Brotherhood
w11:240: The Jews were waiting for a messianic kingdom that would restore the throne of David. In June of A.D. 26, preaching his first full public sermon in the synagogue at Capernaum, Jesus proclaimed an entirely different kingdom.
w11:244: The price of entry was simple too.
w11:248: And the way to greatness in this kingdom runs opposite to the world's way.
w11:252: That day the synagogue audience split three ways: a third believed, a third rejected him, and the rest thought he was out of his mind (137:8.18).
w11:254: A family rather than a kingdom
w11:256: Jesus knew that "kingdom" was not the best vessel for his message. He wanted to recast it in the language of family.
w11:264: Between a king and his subjects there are command and obedience; between a father and his children there are love and trust. Children of the same Father are brothers and sisters to one another. The brotherhood of man follows naturally from the fatherhood of God.
w11:266: The shape of the gospel of the kingdom — the fatherhood of God, the sonship of man, and the brotherhood of man (arranged by the author from 142:7.4 and 170:2)
w11:268: Jesus also taught that the kingdom has two phases.
w11:274: The kingdom is both an experience we enter now by faith and a goal still to be fulfilled. The ascent from the mansion worlds to Paradise that we saw in Week 6 is the road into its second phase.
w11:276: The religion of authority and the religion of the spirit
w11:278: As opposition grew in Galilee, Jesus helped his apostles tell two kinds of religion apart.
w11:282: The religion of authority and the religion of the spirit (arranged by the author from 155:6.2-9)
w11:287: Divides and sets them against each other
w11:289: Grows in the joy and liberty of service
w11:293: The Urantia Book also speaks frankly about how Jesus' gospel was handed on afterward. In the zeal to exalt his person, the message he brought was obscured.
w11:297: That message shows itself best in his life rather than in his sermons.
w11:301: The last paper of the book, on the faith of Jesus, sums up what he asks of us. Here is one line in advance of what we will look at closely in Week 12.
w11:305: In the end, what the Creator showed by becoming a son of man comes down to one thing: God is our Father, and we can believe in Him the way Jesus did.
w11:308: **A common misunderstanding**: The kingdom of heaven is a political, earthly state that will one day come down from the sky and be set up.
w11:309: **What The Urantia Book says**: Jesus said the kingdom is wherever the spirit of God teaches and leads the human soul (137:8.9). We enter it now by faith, and it is fulfilled in heaven (170:2.18-20). He did not connect the kingdom with a second coming to earth (170:2.10), and he expressed its core in the family language of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man (142:7.4).
w11:313: **Personalized Adjuster**: a Thought Adjuster that has finished its mission and gained an independent personality. Jesus' Adjuster was personalized at his baptism and became chief of the Adjusters of Nebadon.
w11:314: **Kingdom of heaven**: a family relationship with God that begins in the human soul seeking to do His will and is fulfilled in heaven.
w11:315: **Brotherhood of man**: the teaching that all people are children of the same Father and so brothers and sisters to one another.
w11:316: **Religion of the spirit**: religion grounded not in authority or creed but in the personal experience of knowing God.
w11:320: The Creator Son Michael became the full sovereign of Nebadon after seven bestowals in the likeness of his own creatures. The bestowals gave him "understanding mercy."
w11:321: In the seventh bestowal he came as a helpless baby and gave himself wholly to the will of the Universal Father. He was God incarnate in man.
w11:322: Jesus grew up with ordinary parents, lost his father at fourteen, and was spiritually disciplined as the head of the household caring for his family.
w11:323: On the Mediterranean journey he met hundreds of people one by one without making himself known. He is not a model to copy but the living way from man to God.
w11:324: He won his sovereignty on Mount Hermon, and at the baptism in the Jordan his Adjuster returned personalized, ending his purely human life.
w11:325: The gospel of the kingdom is the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man. The kingdom is already present wherever the spirit of God leads the human soul.
w11:326: The religion of authority demands uniformity of belief; the religion of the spirit asks only unity of experience and allows for diversity.
w11:330: How does the idea that even a Son of God gained "understanding mercy" through experience (119:0.4) change the way you see the God you pray to?
w11:331: If you measured one habit of your religious life by the young carpenter's three questions (126:2.5), what answers would come out?
w11:332: What does Jesus' preference for the language of "family" over "kingdom" (142:7.4, 170:2.12) ask of the way you treat other people?
w11:336: Papers 171–196 — the entry into Jerusalem and the final week, the cross, the resurrection and morontia appearances, Pentecost, and the faith of Jesus
w12:1: Morning Beyond the Cross, and Today
w12:2: Paper 172:3 · Papers 179–182 · Paper 186:5 · Papers 187–188 · Papers 189–194 · Paper 196:0–2
w12:3: This week's map — through the final week, past the cross and the empty tomb to Pentecost, and at last to the faith of Jesus
w12:6: This week we read the last chapter of Jesus' life on earth. A single week holds it all: the Sunday he rode into Jerusalem on a donkey, the supper in the upper room, the prayer in Gethsemane, the cross on Friday, and the empty tomb before dawn on Sunday. The Urantia Book reads the cross not as an offering that calms God's anger but as a revelation of the Father's love, and it explains the resurrection not as the revival of a corpse but as a morontia resurrection. After the nineteen appearances, the ascension, and the outpouring of the Spirit of Truth at Pentecost, the book closes by inviting the reader into the religion of Jesus rather than a religion about Jesus — a life that shares his own faith.
w12:11: When we sort through an old bundle of letters, the last one often stays with us longest. Years of news and feeling seem to gather into that single page, and in its final lines we learn what the writer cherished most.
w12:13: The last dozen or so papers of Part IV of The Urantia Book are a letter of that kind. The thirty-odd years we followed last week come together in one week. Jesus shares a final meal with his friends, prays alone, is put on trial, and dies on a cross. Then, on the morning of the third day, the story does not end; it begins again.
w12:15: This is also the final week of this guide. Over twelve weeks we started at the center of the universe, passed through the local universe, and came down to this small planet. Now we watch the end of the life that the Maker of that universe lived as a man, and we ask what that life has left for us today.
w12:17: 1. The Final Week — From the Entry to the Upper Room
w12:21: On Sunday, April 2, A.D. 30, Jesus left Bethany for Jerusalem. He had always held back the crowds who wanted to hail him as Messiah, but this time he chose to enter the city openly.
w12:25: He chose with care the manner of his coming.
w12:29: The people were waiting for a liberator who would drive out Rome. By choosing a donkey instead of a horse, Jesus showed in his own person that his kingdom was not a kingdom of the sword. When the cheering crowd reached the brow of Olivet, he stopped and wept.
w12:33: The welcome was loud, but the book says its roots were shallow.
w12:37: Each day of the week that followed grew heavier. On Monday he cleansed the temple, and on Tuesday he taught there for the last time. On Wednesday he rested alone in the hills, and on Thursday evening he shared the last supper in the upper room.
w12:39: The final week — from the Sunday of the entry to the Sunday of the resurrection (arranged by the author from Papers 172–189)
w12:41: A New Commandment in the Upper Room
w12:43: On Thursday night in the upper room, Jesus passed the bread and the cup to the eleven apostles and established the "remembrance supper," the rite that later became the church's communion. The book explains its meaning this way.
w12:47: What matters is less the form of bread and cup than a mind awake to his presence. Jesus had a reason for using symbols rather than a precise formula.
w12:51: After the supper he left them a final charge.
w12:55: The old commandment said to love one's neighbor as oneself. The new one changes the measure: love as Jesus has loved. The same section adds that this love is not a heavy duty.
w12:61: That night, at the foot of the Mount of Olives, Jesus bowed down to pray three times. He asked that the cup might pass, yet in the end he chose the Father's will.
w12:65: In this scene Jesus does not look like a superman. He sweats, and he longs for his friends to keep watch with him. Yet the heart of this man lays hold of the Father's will by faith.
w12:69: The calm he showed the next day was won on this night.
w12:71: 2. The True Meaning of the Cross — Not Atonement but a Revelation of Love
w12:75: Early on Friday Jesus stood before Pilate, and at about half past nine in the morning he was nailed to a cross at Golgotha between two thieves. Just before three in the afternoon he cried, "It is finished," and breathed his last. The book sums up that death in these words.
w12:79: Was this death, then, something God had planned? Many people have been taught so. The Urantia Book answers plainly otherwise.
w12:87: Church tradition often speaks of "substitutionary atonement." In this view human sin made God angry, someone had to bear the penalty in our place before forgiveness was possible, and Jesus paid that price. Paper 188 takes up this frame directly.
w12:91: The reason lies in who God is. As we saw in Week 2, God is above all a Father. The picture of a monarch who is satisfied only once a penalty has been paid does not fit the Father whom Jesus revealed.
w12:95: This does not mean that Jesus has nothing to do with salvation. The book simply suggests a better name for him.
w12:99: What matters, the book adds, is not the death itself but the way he met it.
w12:103: Where the Father's Love Is Shown
w12:105: What, then, is the cross? Section 5 of Paper 188 helps us see the same event through different eyes.
w12:109: The picture of a courtroom gives way to the picture of a family. A father does not extract payment from his son. The cross is not a place where a debt is settled but a place where love is shown going all the way to the end.
w12:117: The cross is also a comfort to those who suffer, because the Creator Himself has passed through human pain.
w12:121: The book gathers up the whole section in a single sentence.
w12:125: Two ways of seeing the cross — the courtroom frame and the family frame (arranged by the author from 188:4–5)
w12:128: **A common misunderstanding**: God was angry at sin and forgives people only after receiving the blood of His Son. Or, the opposite: since The Urantia Book rejects the doctrine of atonement, the cross was a meaningless accident.
w12:129: **What The Urantia Book says**: It was man who planned the cross (186:5.2), and the Father required nothing (188:5.11). God loved people just as much before the life of Jesus (186:5.6). Yet the cross carries great meaning. It is a revelation to the whole universe of the Father's love and the Son's mercy, and Jesus is truly a savior (188:4.7).
w12:133: Jesus said, "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends" (John 15:13, KJV). Paper 188 goes a step further: Jesus had a love that was willing to lay down his life even for his enemies (188:5.7). The confession "God is love" (1 John 4:8) also meets this book's reading of the cross as a revelation of love. Where Hebrews explains the cross in the language of priestly sacrifice, however, this book offers a different interpretation.
w12:136: 3. The Empty Tomb and Nineteen Appearances
w12:140: At two minutes past three on Sunday morning, Jesus rose from the tomb. Yet the resurrection the book describes is not a dead body breathing again. Jesus rose in a "morontia" form, a body in between, neither material nor spirit — the very kind of body that people wear when they awaken after death on the mansion worlds we met in Week 6.
w12:144: Why, then, was the tomb empty? Jesus' physical body was not used in the resurrection.
w12:150: The empty tomb is not the proof of the resurrection but a fact that came with it. The real evidence is the experience of those who met the living Master. This account does not diminish the resurrection; rather, it ties it to the future of each one of us.
w12:158: The first witnesses were five women who had come to the tomb. Mary Magdalene took the stranger for the gardener and asked where he had taken the Master's body.
w12:162: His form had changed, but the voice that called her by name was the same. The risen Jesus went first to those who grieved. Women and ordinary believers set out with the news before the doubting apostles did. In the end, the evidence for the resurrection was encounters like these.
w12:168: Over the next forty days Jesus appeared in many places to many groups.
w12:172: A few things stand out in the list. He appeared not only in Jerusalem but in Galilee, at Sychar in Samaria, at Tyre in Phoenicia, and as far away as Philadelphia and Alexandria. He appeared not only to the apostles but to women, to his family, and to Greeks and Samaritans. From the very beginning the news of the resurrection crossed the boundaries of a single people.
w12:174: The nineteen morontia appearances of the risen Jesus (arranged by the author from Papers 190–193)
w12:178: His brother James; his earthly family
w12:182: Abner and Lazarus, with about 150 others
w12:185: Ten apostles; eleven apostles; over 500 believers
w12:188: From the upper room to Olivet
w12:191: **Morontia resurrection**: Not the revival of a dead body, but rising in the likeness of a morontia personality, like those who awaken on the mansion worlds.
w12:192: **Morontia appearance**: A time when the risen Jesus, with special help, became visible to human eyes. There were nineteen in all.
w12:193: **World of the Cross**: The name by which neighboring planets know Urantia, because the Creator Son was crucified here.
w12:196: 4. Pentecost and the Spirit of Truth
w12:198: Farewell and Gift on the Same Day
w12:200: On the morning of Thursday, May 18, Jesus stood with the eleven apostles on the slope of Olivet. When they knelt in a circle around him of their own accord, he spoke his last words.
w12:206: The book does not dramatize the ascension. The remarkable thing happened that afternoon. On the very day of the ascension, the promised spirit came to the one hundred and twenty gathered in the upper room in Jerusalem.
w12:210: From resurrection to Pentecost — nineteen appearances in forty days, and the ascension and Pentecost on the same day (arranged by the author from Papers 190–194)
w12:214: The book calls this spirit the Spirit of Truth, or the "new teacher." It is the same spirit whose name we only glimpsed in Week 1. What does the Spirit of Truth do?
w12:218: The Spirit of Truth does not announce itself through dramatic experiences.
w12:222: The sign of the spirit's presence is not a mysterious feeling but coming to know Jesus more closely. Nor did this spirit come only to the apostles or to a special few.
w12:226: At Pentecost, women and men, Jesus' family and ordinary disciples, all received the same gift. No special place or ceremony was needed.
w12:232: The book describes what Pentecost changed in these words.
w12:236: This spirit does not lead people to flee from life; it sends them back into the middle of it. Jesus himself lived that way.
w12:240: The picture of evolutionary and revealed religion that we saw in Week 1 is completed here. The hand reaching up from below and the hand stretched down from above meet within the human heart. Together with the Thought Adjuster of Week 10 and the Holy Spirit of the Universe Mother Spirit, the Spirit of Truth makes up the threefold gift of spirit at work within us.
w12:243: **Remembrance supper**: The rite of bread and cup that Jesus established in the upper room on his last night; the believer's symbolic rendezvous with Michael.
w12:244: **Ascension**: The risen Jesus' return to the Father at the close of his forty-day morontia career, on the Mount of Olives on May 18, A.D. 30.
w12:245: **Pentecost**: The name of a Jewish festival. In The Urantia Book it refers to the day of the ascension, when the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all believers.
w12:248: 5. The Faith of Jesus — From a Religion about Jesus to the Religion of Jesus
w12:250: When the Facts Took the Place of the Message
w12:252: Filled with the joy of Pentecost, the apostles went out into the streets to preach. But what did they proclaim? Paper 194 makes a quiet but weighty observation. Instead of the gospel Jesus had taught, they began to preach facts about Jesus, above all the resurrection.
w12:256: Jesus proclaimed that God is Father and that all people are brothers and sisters. The apostles proclaimed that Jesus had risen. Both are precious, but they are not the same. The first is the faith Jesus himself lived by; the second is belief in the person of Jesus. Paper 196 states the difference this way.
w12:262: The religion of Jesus and the religion about Jesus (arranged by the author from 194:0.4 and 196:1–2)
w12:265: The fatherhood of God, the brotherhood of man
w12:266: The personal religious experience of the Jesus of Galilee
The religious experience of the apostles, especially Paul
w12:269: Doing the Father's will and serving others
The fellowship of believers and the church
w12:273: Where does the religion of Jesus begin? The opening of Paper 196 portrays Jesus' own faith.
w12:277: That faith resembled the heart of a child.
w12:281: Yet it was never childish. And Jesus did not keep this faith to himself.
w12:285: The difference between "believing in Jesus" and "believing with Jesus" is the key to this week. In the first, Jesus becomes someone we look at; in the second, he becomes an elder brother who walks beside us. Paper 196 urges again and again that the human Jesus not be lost.
w12:291: So there is one more tomb this week. What, then, does it mean to follow him?
w12:295: This is not an easy road. It was not easy even for Jesus.
w12:299: There is no need to become a carpenter or to walk the roads of Galilee. It is enough to live each day, wherever we are, with the trust he had in the Father, and to look at our neighbors with the eyes that saw every person as precious. The book calls this the most valuable knowledge of all.
w12:303: The seven stages of faith-consciousness Jesus passed through — from the arrival of the Adjuster to the Father's final embrace (196:1.6–13)
w12:307: The last section of the last paper of The Urantia Book ends with where human thinking about God finally arrives. Our twelve-week journey comes to rest here as well.
w12:311: In the first week we unfolded a route map. Every line on that map leads at last to a single station: the Father who loves us, and the one man who lived that love to the very end. After the book is closed, one question remains — whether to share his faith today in our own lives.
w12:314: **A common misunderstanding**: Because it stresses "the religion of Jesus," The Urantia Book sees Jesus as merely a fine human teacher.
w12:315: **What The Urantia Book says**: The book calls it "the great mistake" to think of Jesus as entirely human or as only divine (196:2.3). He is truly man and truly God. The point is that in exalting the divine Christ we must not lose the man Jesus of Galilee, who struggled by faith (196:1.1–2).
w12:319: Jesus entered Jerusalem on a donkey as a king of peace, and in the upper room he left the remembrance supper and the new commandment to love "even as I have loved you."
w12:320: It was man, not God, who planned the cross. Jesus did not die as an offering to appease the wrath of God (186:5.2, 188:4.1).
w12:321: The cross is a revelation of love that places the relation between God and man on a family basis, and Jesus is truly a savior (188:4.7, 188:5.1).
w12:322: Jesus rose not in the flesh but in morontia form. The empty tomb is a fact attached to the resurrection, not its truth.
w12:323: The risen Jesus appeared nineteen times over forty days, and on May 18, the very day of his ascension, the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all believers.
w12:324: Since Pentecost, religion is no longer only man seeking God; it is also God coming to seek man.
w12:325: One may preach a religion about Jesus, but one must live the religion of Jesus. Jesus asks us not to believe in him but to believe with him.
w12:329: When you see the cross as a "family picture" rather than a "courtroom picture," how does your sense of God change?
w12:330: The risen Jesus went first to those who grieved and those who doubted. What scene in your own life does this story echo?
w12:331: If you were to turn the difference between "believing in Jesus" and "believing with Jesus" into one practice for today, what would it be?
w12:335: Closing Words and Appendix 2, "Further Study" — at the end of twelve weeks, choosing which papers to read next from where we now stand
closing:1: Afterword — From Where We Are, Onward
closing:3: We have come a long way in twelve weeks. In the first week we stood like a traveler in a strange city before a subway map and unfolded the map of The Urantia Book. Then we met the Universal Father at the center of all things, the Trinity, Paradise and Havona, and the great family of beings who serve the seven superuniverses. We passed through our home universe of Nebadon, the mansion worlds beyond death, the ages of a planet and the Lucifer rebellion, and arrived at the birth of this small world, Urantia, the dawn of humankind, the default in Eden and the road back, and the spirit of God who lives within each person. In the last two weeks we followed the Creator who became a Son of Man, through his life to the cross, the empty tomb and the morning of Pentecost.
closing:5: If all of this had to be said in a single line, it might be this: God is our Father, all people are brothers and sisters, and each one of us is invited on an eternal journey of becoming like Him. The history of stars and planets, the service of angels and Sons, the life of Jesus himself, all point toward this one truth.
closing:7: Twelve weeks are not enough to say that we know The Urantia Book. This guide has taken only a few steps at each crossroads of a book more than two thousand pages long. But now the reader holds a map. Whatever paper you open, you can guess where in the universe, when in history, and on which step of the ascent its story belongs. For a first-time reader, that guess is the greatest help of all.
closing:9: From here, study can go two ways. One is to read the book straight through from the beginning; the other is to follow the topics that draw you and read paper by paper. Either way, read a section a day and do not hurry. Reading alone is good, but reading with friends is better. The same sentence looks different through other eyes, and those differences lead us to deeper understanding. The next pages offer a guide to further reading.
closing:11: Knowledge is a lamp that lights the road, but the strength to walk it comes from fellowship with the living God. What The Urantia Book most wants is not that its readers know the book, but that they know the Father it points to. May these twelve weeks have been the first step of that fellowship. From where we are, onward.

reading:23: **A section a day**: a paper is usually divided into several sections. Reading one section a day, slowly, takes you through the whole book in a little over a year.
reading:24: **Mark unfamiliar words and keep going**: new terms are usually explained later. The "New Words" appendix in this book can help too.
reading:25: **Stay with one sentence**: choose one sentence that speaks to you and turn it over for a day. More will stay with you than the number of pages you read.
reading:26: **Read together**: when a study group reads the same section and talks it over, each person sees what they could not see alone.

terms:Adjuster fusion.def: The eternal union of the Thought Adjuster with the human soul. It usually occurs on the mansion worlds, and afterward the eternal career is no longer at risk.

terms:adjutant mind-spirits.def: The seven circuits through which the Mother Spirit works at the level of mind: the spirits of intuition, understanding, courage, knowledge, counsel, worship, and wisdom.

terms:agondonter.def: The name for ascenders from quarantined worlds who believed without seeing and persevered in isolation.

terms:Amadon.def: The Andonite who stood with Van against the rebellion to the end; the outstanding human hero of the Lucifer rebellion.

terms:Ancients of Days.def: Rulers of Trinity origin who govern the superuniverses, three for each superuniverse.

terms:Andon and Fonta.def: The first human twins, born to the Primates about a million years ago; the actual parents of all mankind.

terms:Andonites.def: The primitive race made up of the descendants of Andon and Fonta; the aborigines of Urantia.

terms:Angona.def: A huge system of bodies that passed near our sun about 4.5 billion years ago and, by its gravity, drew out the material of the solar system's planets.

terms:ascending pilgrim.def: The name for a mortal survivor who has been cleared for the progressive ascent toward Paradise.

terms:ascending son.def: A being born on an evolutionary world who attains sonship through experience; human beings belong here.

terms:atonement doctrine.def: The idea that someone must pay the price of sin in our place before God's wrath can be satisfied. The Urantia Book calls it incompatible with the Father whom Jesus revealed.

terms:attribute.def: A trait that shows what kind of Being God is. Papers 2 and 3 treat infinity, immutability, justice, mercy, omnipresence, omniscience, omnipotence and others.

terms:autorevelation.def: Truth made clear in a person's mind through the work of the indwelling Adjuster.

terms:Badonan tribes.def: Descendants of the Andonites living in the highlands of northwestern India, among whom the Sangik family was born.

terms:bestowal.def: The act of a descending Son who is born in the likeness of a creature and lives that life in person.

terms:bestowal parents.def: Joseph and Mary, the earthly parents of Jesus. Gabriel chose them as an ordinary couple with an ideal combination of qualities.

terms:bestowal Son.def: A Paradise Son who bestows himself on an evolutionary world. To Urantia the Creator Son Michael came in person.

terms:biologic uplifters.def: Another name for the Material Sons and Daughters. They share their bloodline with the evolutionary races to raise humanity in body and mind.

terms:Bright and Morning Star.def: The chief executive of a local universe, the first being created jointly by the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit. In Nebadon, Gabriel of Salvington.

terms:brotherhood of man.def: The teaching that all people are children of the same Father and so brothers and sisters, shown in loving service.

terms:Conjoint Actor.def: Another name for the Infinite Spirit, meaning the one who carries out in action the united will of the Father and the Son.

terms:corporeal staff (the one hundred).def: One hundred ascendant citizens of Jerusem who came with the Planetary Prince, took on material bodies, and taught mankind. Forty remained loyal in the rebellion.

terms:Corps of the Finality.def: The corps into which ascending mortals who reach Paradise are mustered, beginning their eternal service.

terms:Creator Son.def: A Paradise Son of God who makes and rules a local universe. Michael of Nebadon, the Creator Son of our universe, came to this world as Jesus.

terms:cult.def: A system of rites and symbols that preserves religious feeling and loyalty. It began with the ghost cult and grew into the sacraments.

terms:Dalamatia.def: The headquarters city founded by the Planetary Prince Caligastia in Mesopotamia and mankind's first school; it sank beneath the sea after the rebellion.

terms:dark gravity bodies.def: Enormous bodies that encircle Havona in two belts and balance the gravity of Paradise. They neither reflect nor absorb light.

terms:dawn mammals.def: The first stage of man's direct animal ancestry, which appeared by sudden mutation from the lemur type.

terms:default.def: Failure to keep a covenant and trust. What Adam and Eve did was judged a default, not the sin of rebellion.

terms:descending Son.def: A Son of God created divine from the beginning who comes down to serve the lower worlds.

terms:dispensation.def: A stretch of planetary history opened when a Son of God arrives on a world. A normal world passes through seven ages.

terms:Divine Counselor.def: A high personality of Trinity origin serving in superuniverse administration. Divine Counselors wrote the Foreword, Paper 1, and several other papers.

terms:Divinington.def: One of the Father's worlds around Paradise and the home of the Thought Adjusters. After death the Adjuster goes there for a time.

terms:Edentia.def: Headquarters of the constellation of Norlatiadek, where on seventy training worlds ascenders learn the group ethics of living with other beings.

terms:emergency Son.def: A Son bestowed specially in a crisis not provided for in the normal plan. Machiventa Melchizedek is an example.

terms:epochal revelation.def: A great revelation given by celestial beings for an entire age. Urantia has received five.

terms:Eternal Son.def: The second Person of the Paradise Trinity, who fully shares the spiritual nature of the Universal Father.

terms:evil.def: The misadaptation of plans and the maladjustment of techniques. It can arise even from good motives and is distinct from sin, which is deliberate transgression.

terms:evolutionary religion.def: Humanity's circuitous search for truth, beginning in fear of the unknown.

terms:faith.def: The level belief reaches when it actually governs the way a person lives. Beliefs can be held by a group, but faith grows only in the individual heart.

terms:fatherhood of God.def: The truth that God is the loving Father of every person, the first pillar of Jesus' gospel.

terms:First Source and Center.def: The name for God used throughout the universe, meaning that all things come from Him and revolve around Him.

terms:first-stage spirit.def: The first spirit status, gained on completing the morontia course of the local universe, just before departing for the training worlds of the superuniverse.

terms:Foreword.def: The guide to the meaning of terms at the front of the book (Paper 0), written by a Divine Counselor of Orvonton.

terms:fusion.def: The eternal union of a surviving human soul with the Thought Adjuster. Once fused, the two can never again be separated.

terms:Gabriel vs. Lucifer.def: The case pending before the superuniverse court on Uversa that deals with the final disposition of the rebel leaders.

terms:Garden of Eden.def: The garden prepared by Van and Amadon on a peninsula of the eastern Mediterranean, the first headquarters of Adam and Eve. It later sank beneath the sea.

terms:God-consciousness.def: The intellectual capacity for knowing God, the first sign of the presence of the indwelling Adjuster.

terms:gospel of the kingdom.def: Jesus' own message: the fatherhood of God and the sonship-brotherhood of men.

terms:grand universe.def: The presently organized and inhabited creation, made up of the central universe Havona and the seven superuniverses. It holds about seven trillion inhabitable worlds.

terms:great circuit of love.def: The circle in which love from the Father passes through each person to his or her brothers and on to the Supreme (117:6.10).

terms:guardian of destiny.def: A seraphic guardian personally assigned to one human being, who walks with that person through life.

terms:Havona.def: The central universe of a billion perfect worlds surrounding Paradise. It did not evolve but was created perfect from the beginning.

terms:Holy Spirit.def: In this book, the spiritual presence of the local universe Mother Spirit. It takes the worshiping mind into the spirit circuits.

terms:Immanuel.def: A high being who represents the Paradise Trinity in Nebadon. He looked after the universe during Michael's bestowal and gave him his charge before it began.

terms:immutability.def: The unchanging nature and purpose of God. Divine immutability does not imply immobility.

terms:incarnation.def: A divine being being born in a human body. How it happens remains an eternal mystery.

terms:indwelling.def: Living within. The Adjuster indwells the human mind, not the brain.

terms:Infinite Spirit.def: The third Person of the Paradise Trinity, also called the Conjoint Actor, and the source of all mind.

terms:inhabited world.def: A planet where mortals with will live. Urantia is the 606th inhabited world of Satania.

terms:institutionalized religion.def: Living religious experience hardened into a focus on organization and creeds. Paper 99 calls sectarianism its disease.

terms:Jerusem.def: Capital of the local system of Satania, where ascenders who finish the mansion worlds become citizens and learn representative government.

terms:Joshua ben Joseph.def: Joshua the son of Joseph, the Hebrew name The Urantia Book uses for Jesus.

terms:kingdom of heaven.def: The kingdom found wherever the spirit of God teaches and leads the human soul. It is entered now by faith and fulfilled in heaven.

terms:Lanonandek Sons.def: The order of local universe Sons who serve as System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes. Because they come close to mortals, they also run a greater risk of going astray.

terms:Life Carriers.def: Local universe Sons who design life, plant it on planets, and remain for long ages to foster its development.

terms:life implantation.def: The planting of the original life patterns on a planet by the Life Carriers. On Urantia it took place in three places at once, 550 million years ago.

terms:life-modification world.def: A planet on which experiments in changing and improving the standard life designs are permitted. Urantia is such a world, so its life is unique.

terms:light and life.def: The settled final age an evolutionary world reaches after all its dispensations; it widens in seven stages from a planet to a superuniverse.

terms:local universe.def: A unit of about ten million worlds made and ruled by one Creator Son. Our local universe is Nebadon.

terms:Lucifer manifesto.def: Lucifer's declaration of rebellion on Jerusem, also called the Declaration of Liberty. It attacked the reality of the Father, Michael's government, and the ascension plan.

terms:Lucifer rebellion.def: The rebellion raised about two hundred thousand years ago by Lucifer, System Sovereign of Satania, against the rule of Michael.

terms:Machiventa Melchizedek.def: One of the twelve Melchizedeks in charge of Urantia. He appeared at Salem in human form 1,973 years before the birth of Jesus and brought the third epochal revelation.

terms:Magisterial Son.def: A Paradise Son of the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit, called an Avonal, who judges planetary ages and sometimes bestows himself.

terms:Mansion World Teachers.def: Glorified cherubim and sanobim, once helpers of the guardian angels, who teach ascenders in the schools of thinking, feeling, and doing.

terms:mansion worlds.def: The seven satellites circling the first transition world of Jerusem, where survivors first awaken and are trained after death.

terms:Master Spirit.def: One of the primary personalities of the Infinite Spirit; the seven Master Spirits express the seven associations of the three Deities, and each oversees one superuniverse.

terms:master universe.def: The whole universe: Paradise-Havona, the seven superuniverses, and the four outer space levels still being organized.

terms:Material Son and Daughter.def: The Adam and Eve who come to a planet to uplift its races biologically.

terms:Melchizedek receivers.def: The twelve Melchizedeks who took charge of Urantia after the rebellion of the Planetary Prince.

terms:Melchizedek Sons.def: The eldest-son order of the local universe. They lead the education of ascenders and step in as "emergency Sons" on worlds in crisis.

terms:Michael of Nebadon.def: The Creator Son who made Nebadon and lived on Urantia as Jesus of Nazareth. To our universe he is, to all practical intents and purposes, God.

terms:midwayer.def: A being between humans and angels who has long lived on this planet. The midwayers wrote Part IV, the life of Jesus.

terms:Mighty Messenger.def: A former ascendant mortal who reached Paradise, was embraced by the Trinity, and now serves in a superuniverse government.

terms:mind gravity.def: The pull that draws all minds and all true intellectual values to the Infinite Spirit.

terms:ministering spirit.def: The angels, children of the Infinite Spirit, who teach and help ascending creatures.

terms:Monmatia.def: The name for our sun and its family of planets, that is, the solar system.

terms:morontia.def: The intermediate level of reality between matter and spirit; after death a person awakens in a morontia body.

terms:morontia appearance.def: A time when the risen Jesus became visible to human eyes. There were nineteen in the forty days before his ascension.

terms:morontia companions.def: Children of the local universe Mother Spirit who welcome, guide, and share leisure with ascenders on the mansion worlds.

terms:morontia resurrection.def: Jesus' rising from the tomb not in the flesh but in the likeness of a morontia personality, like those who are resurrected on the mansion worlds.

terms:mortal.def: A being who faces death, that is, a human being; one of the book's basic terms.

terms:mota.def: Morontia wisdom, higher than human philosophy. On the first mansion world it is studied side by side with sayings of human philosophy.

terms:Mystery Monitor.def: Another name for the Thought Adjuster, the fragment of the Father that indwells the human mind.

terms:Nebadon.def: The name of the local universe we belong to; a young universe growing toward a hundred constellations, ten thousand systems, and ten million inhabited worlds.

terms:new commandment.def: Jesus' final charge, "That you love one another even as I have loved you." It was given not as a duty but as the joy of friendship.

terms:new teacher.def: A name for the Spirit of Truth poured out at Pentecost. It fosters truth and keeps believers from feeling orphaned.

terms:Nodites.def: Descendants of the rebel members of the Planetary Prince's staff, named after their first leader, Nod. They are the eighth race of Urantia.

terms:omnipresence.def: Being present everywhere at the same time (3:1.1).

terms:omniscience / omnipotence.def: Knowing all things and holding all power. Omnipotence does not mean the power to do the ungodlike.

terms:Onagar.def: The great teacher who brought peace to the declining Andonite tribes and led them together in worship of the Breath Giver.

terms:Orvonton.def: The seventh superuniverse, to which we belong. Its headquarters is Uversa, and it is called a universe demonstration of love and mercy.

terms:outer space levels.def: The four concentric levels of space beyond the seven superuniverses, still in the process of being organized.

terms:pair marriage.def: The union of one man and one woman to establish a home of the highest social order; the culmination of the evolution of marriage.

terms:Paradise.def: The eternal Isle at the center of all things, where the Universal Father dwells.

terms:Paradise Trinity.def: The eternal Deity union of the three persons, Father, Son, and Spirit. It is not a gathering of three Gods but a single union of Deity.

terms:Pentecost.def: The name of a Jewish festival. In this book it refers to the day of the ascension, when the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all believers.

terms:personality.def: What makes a being self-conscious, able to choose, and able to share fellowship with other personalities. Only the Universal Father bestows it.

terms:personality circuit.def: The circuit through which the Universal Father makes direct contact with every personality. The worship of all personalities reaches the Father through it.

terms:Personalized Adjuster.def: A Thought Adjuster that has finished its mission and gained an independent personality. Jesus' Adjuster was personalized at his baptism in the Jordan and became chief of the Adjusters of Nebadon.

terms:Planetary Prince.def: The being entrusted with the spiritual government of a planet. Caligastia, the Planetary Prince of Urantia, joined the rebellion.

terms:power directors.def: Beings who, once energy responds to gravity, gather the energies of space and shape them into suns and planets. They work before the Creator Son arrives.

terms:Primates.def: The direct ancestors that came from the mid-mammals and gave birth to the first humans. In this book the word is used in this narrow sense, for man's direct ancestors only.

terms:Providence.def: The interlocking work of celestial beings and divine spirits for the honor of God and the spiritual progress of His children.

terms:quarantine.def: The measure that cut the planets involved in the rebellion off from the universe circuits. Urantia is a quarantined world.

terms:religion about Jesus.def: A religion that makes the risen and glorified Christ the object of worship; it grew up after Pentecost through the apostles and Paul.

terms:religion of authority.def: Religion that leans on the authority of tradition and records and demands uniformity of belief. It tends to divide people and harden into lifeless creeds.

terms:religion of Jesus.def: The personal faith Jesus himself lived: doing the Father's will and serving one's fellows.

terms:religion of the spirit.def: Religion grounded not in authority or creed but in the personal experience of knowing God. It asks only unity of experience and allows diversity of belief.

terms:remembrance supper.def: The rite of bread and cup that Jesus established in the upper room on his last night; the believer's symbolic rendezvous with Michael.

terms:resurrection halls.def: The temple of personality assembly at the center of the first mansion world, where Adjuster and soul reunite and the survivor awakens.

terms:revelatory religion.def: Religion propounded by the real spiritual world in response to human longing, marked by belief in a Deity of final value and in survival after death.

terms:Salvington.def: The headquarters (capital) of the local universe of Nebadon, an architectural sphere where Michael and the Universe Mother Spirit reside.

terms:Sangik races.def: The six colored races born about half a million years ago into one Sangik family of the Badonan tribes: the red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and indigo races.

terms:Satania.def: The local system to which Urantia belongs; its capital is Jerusem, and it now has 619 inhabited worlds.

terms:savior.def: A name for Jesus, not as one who paid a ransom but as one whose life and death made the way of salvation more clear and certain.

terms:second garden.def: The new home Adam and Eve founded by the Euphrates after the default. There the Sethite priests carried on their teachings.

terms:seraphim.def: Angels created by the Universe Mother Spirit, the ministering spirits of time who help mortals most closely. They work in pairs.

terms:seventh bestowal.def: Michael's final bestowal: the life he lived on Urantia as the mortal man Jesus of Nazareth, following the will of the Universal Father.

terms:sleeping survivors.def: Those without a personal guardian angel, who rest unconscious until the end of an age and then awaken together as a group.

terms:Son of Man.def: The title Jesus chose for himself. As a youth he read it in the Book of Enoch and took it as the name of his mission.

terms:soul.def: The morontia reality born and growing out of the relationship between the mind and the indwelling Adjuster; it survives death.

terms:Source and Center.def: The origin from which all things come and to which they return. The Father, Son, and Spirit are called the First, Second, and Third Source and Center.

terms:spirit ascension.def: The risen Jesus' return to the Father at the close of his morontia career, on the Mount of Olives on May 18, A.D. 30.

terms:spirit gravity.def: The pull that draws all spiritual realities and values to the Eternal Son. It responds to quality, not quantity, and does not weaken with distance.

terms:Spirit of Truth.def: The spirit poured out by the Creator Son, which helps people recognize truth.

terms:spirit of wisdom.def: The seventh of the seven adjutant mind-spirits, which turns worship away from natural objects toward the God of nature.

terms:spirit of worship.def: The sixth of the seven adjutant mind-spirits, which constantly stirred the urge to worship even in primitive minds.

terms:spiritual unity.def: Oneness that comes not from thinking alike but from each person's awareness of the Father's indwelling spirit and the shared desire to do His will.

terms:supernaphim / seconaphim / seraphi.def: The angelic hosts of the central universe, the superuniverses, and the local universes respectively; together they form an unbroken chain of ministry.

terms:superuniverse.def: One of the seven great creations evolving in time and space, each holding about a trillion inhabitable worlds.

terms:Supreme Being.def: The God who grows through experience together with the universes of time and space. Standing alone, He is called "the Supreme."

terms:System Sovereign.def: The Lanonandek Son who governs a local system of about a thousand worlds. Lucifer was the System Sovereign of Satania.

terms:Thought Adjuster.def: A fragment of the Father's spirit that God sends to dwell in the human mind. The Foreword calls it "a fragment of God."

terms:Thought Changer.def: The name given to the Adjuster from its arrival until a person is about twenty years old.

terms:Thought Controller.def: The name given to the Adjuster from the age of discretion (about forty) until deliverance from the flesh.

terms:Trinitized Son.def: A Son of God who has passed through a trinitizing experience or has been embraced by the Trinity.

terms:Trinity Teacher Son.def: A Paradise Son of the Father, Son, and Spirit, called a Daynal, who teaches throughout the universes.

terms:Universal Father.def: The God of all creation and the First Source and Center. It is the name The Urantia Book uses most often for God.

terms:Universe Mother Spirit.def: The daughter of the Infinite Spirit who creates and governs a local universe together with the Creator Son. She is also called the Divine Minister and the Creative Spirit.

terms:Urantia.def: The name by which our planet, the earth, is known in the universe. The title The Urantia Book comes from it.

terms:Urantia Papers.def: The fifth epochal revelation: not the work of a single personality but a composite presentation by many beings.

terms:Van.def: Chairman of the supreme council of the one hundred, who denounced Caligastia's rebellion and remained loyal to the end.

terms:violet race.def: The race made up of the descendants of Adam and Eve, also called the Adamites. Blending with the Nodites and others, they later became the Andites.

terms:Vorondadek Sons.def: The order of local universe Sons who govern the constellations; also called Constellation Fathers.

terms:will creature.def: An intelligent being able to choose and decide for itself. Human beings are will creatures.

terms:World of the Cross.def: The name by which neighboring planets know Urantia, because the Creator Son was crucified here.

terms:worship.def: A response offered to the Universal Father that asks nothing for oneself and simply delights in God as He is.
